# Trading Brief — 2026-08-06

# Section 3: Horizon Scan — Regulatory & Catalyst Events

_Scanned: FDA Advisory Committee Calendar, PCAC, Federal Register, DEA Marijuana Rescheduling, DEA Telemedicine, FDA Compounding Policy, Psychedelic Drug Development, GLP-1 Compounding Enforcement, Congressional Hearings, PDUFA Calendar._

---

## 1. DEA Marijuana Rescheduling — ALJ Briefs Due August 17, Recommendation Imminent

**Event Type:** P1 — Regulatory re-scheduling
**Future Catalyst Date:** August 17, 2026 (post-hearing briefs deadline) → ALJ recommendation weeks after → DEA final rule
**Time Remaining:** ~1.5 weeks (briefs), then 4-8 weeks for ALJ recommendation

**What happened:** The DEA marijuana rescheduling hearing concluded July 15, 2026 after 11 hearing days. Chief ALJ Derek C. Julius ordered post-hearing briefs due no later than August 17, 2026. Once briefs are submitted, the ALJ will issue a recommendation to the DEA Administrator, who then issues a final rule. The government's case for Schedule III remained intact through cross-examination — opposition testimony largely addressed state-market harms rather than statutory Schedule III criteria.

**Why it matters:** This is the closest federal cannabis reform has ever gotten. The hearing is done; the record is built. The ALJ recommendation is the next domino. If the ALJ recommends Schedule III (likely given the government's stronger statutory case), DEA would issue a final rule moving marijuana to Schedule III — unlocking banking access, 280E tax relief, and institutional investment. Cannabis stocks are quietly drifting (MSOS at $4.03, down from highs) with low retail attention. The asymmetric setup: a Schedule III decision could trigger a multi-week rerating of the entire sector, while further delay is already partially priced.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| MSOS | ETF — multi-state cannabis operators | Direct proxy for Schedule III thesis; 280E relief = earnings re-rating |
| TLRY | Tilray — cannabis + alcohol + pharma | Largest LP by revenue; rescheduling expands US market access |
| CGC | Canopy Growth — cannabis + bio-pharma | US listing proxy; Balance Sheet stressed but highest beta to rescheduling |

**What would prove this wrong:** ALJ recommends against rescheduling (low probability — government's statutory case held up). Political intervention or litigation injunction from states (Nebraska, Idaho, Indiana, Louisiana are opposing parties). Congressional action preempting the regulatory process.

**If this plays out:** Schedule III final rule by Q4 2026/Q1 2027. MSOS could see 30-50% move on the announcement. 280E tax savings alone would transform multi-state operator P&Ls from losses to profits.

**Key signals to watch:**
- August 17: Post-hearing briefs filed (check DEA docket)
- September-October: ALJ recommendation window
- Any signals from DOJ/DEA leadership on timing
- Safe Banking Act re-introduction in Congress (parallel catalyst)

**Sources:**
- [DEA Marijuana Rescheduling Page](https://www.dea.gov/marijuana-rescheduling-regulatory-actions) — Hearing June 29 - July 15, 2026; interested parties named
- [Vicente LLP Analysis](https://vicentellp.com/insights/final-week-dea-marijuana-rescheduling-hearing-ends-opposition-builds-appellate-record-but-leaves-statutory-gaps/) — Post-hearing briefs due Aug 17; government's stronger statutory case
- [Federal Register Notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/04/28/2026-08177/schedules-of-controlled-substances-rescheduling-of-marijuana) — Official hearing notice

---

## 2. FDA Psychedelic Public Hearing (Sept 14) + Compass Pathways NDA Filing (Q4 2026)

**Event Type:** P1 — Drug policy + pipeline catalyst
**Future Catalyst Date:** September 14, 2026 (FDA public hearing) → Q4 2026 (Compass NDA final submission) → 1-2 month Priority Review (voucher awarded)
**Time Remaining:** ~5.5 weeks (hearing), ~4 months (NDA filing)

**What happened:** FDA published a Federal Register notice (July 14, 2026) announcing a hybrid public hearing on "Considerations for Potential Future Therapeutic Use of Psychedelic Drugs" for September 14, 2026. Comments accepted until October 5, 2026. This follows EO 14401 (April 2026) directing FDA to accelerate psychedelic drug review. Separately, Compass Pathways (CMPS) has a rolling NDA submission underway for COMP360 (synthetic psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression), with final submission targeted for Q4 2026. FDA awarded a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher that could compress review to 1-2 months post-filing. Six-month Phase 3 data released in 2026 confirmed rapid and durable efficacy.

**Why it matters:** This is a two-stage catalyst chain. The September 14 hearing is the first major FDA public forum on psychedelic therapeutics — it will generate significant media coverage and set the tone for the regulatory pathway. If the hearing signals a supportive FDA posture (likely given EO 14401), it de-risks the Compass NDA timeline. A Priority Review voucher means that once the NDA is filed in Q4, an approval decision could come within 1-2 months — potentially by end of 2026 or early 2027. CMPS is at $13.58, up significantly from $3.97 (52-week low) but well off the $15.40 June high. Volume has cooled. The first FDA-approved psychedelic would be a landmark event with massive narrative power.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| CMPS | Compass Pathways — COMP360 psilocybin for TRD | Direct NDA filing; Priority Review voucher; first-mover on FDA-approved psychedelic |
| MNMD | Mind Medicine — MDMA/lsd pipeline | Sector sympathy; also EO 14401 beneficiary |

**What would prove this wrong:** FDA hearing reveals significant safety concerns or restrictive framework. Compass NDA filing slips to 2027. Phase 3 data challenges emerge in peer review. Priority Review voucher scope narrowed.

**If this plays out:** COMP360 becomes the first FDA-approved psychedelic therapy. Compass launches commercially in 2027. CMPS market cap ($1.9B today) could 3-5x on approval given the TRD market size (~5M patients in the US) and novelty premium. Sector-wide rerating for psychedelic stocks.

**Key signals to watch:**
- September 14: FDA public hearing tone and attendance
- October 5: Comment period closes — institutional comments signal direction
- Q3/Q4: Compass NDA submission progress updates
- Any FDA guidance documents published post-hearing

**Sources:**
- [Federal Register — Psychedelic Public Hearing Notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/14/2026-14155/considerations-for-potential-future-therapeutic-use-of-psychedelic-drugs-public-hearing-request-for) — Sept 14 hearing, comments to Oct 5
- [FDA Hearing Page](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/fda-meetings-conferences-and-workshops/considerations-potential-future-therapeutic-use-psychedelic-drugs-public-hearing-09142026) — Registration open through Aug 21
- [Compass IR — NDA Rolling Submission](https://ir.compasspathways.com/News--Events-/news/news-details/2026/Compass-Pathways-Announces-FDA-Granted-NDA-Rolling-Review-Request-and-Awarded-Commissioners-National-Priority-Voucher/default.aspx) — Rolling NDA, Priority Voucher, Q4 2026 target
- [White House EO 14401](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/04/accelerating-medical-treatments-for-serious-mental-illness/) — Directive to accelerate psychedelic research and approval

---

## 3. GLP-1 Compounding Exclusion — Final Decision Pending

**Event Type:** P2 — Regulatory enforcement
**Future Catalyst Date:** Final FDA determination expected Q3 2026 (comment period closed June 30, 2026)
**Time Remaining:** ~4-8 weeks for final decision

**What happened:** On April 30, 2026, FDA proposed excluding semaglutide, tirzepatide, and liraglutide from the 503B Bulks List — meaning outsourcing facilities would be prohibited from compounding these GLP-1 drugs. The public comment period closed June 30, 2026. FDA found "no clinical need" for compounding since the shortage has resolved and FDA-approved products (Wegovy, Ozempic, Mounjaro, Zepbound) are available. A final determination is now pending. Once finalized, compounding pharmacies must cease production within a transition period.

**Why it matters:** The compounding industry has been a gray-market competitor to branded GLP-1s, supplying millions of doses. A final exclusion decision would (a) eliminate the compounding workaround, driving patients to branded/prescription channels, and (b) crack down on telehealth companies built on compounded GLP-1s. HIMS (Hims & Hers Health) has been a major distributor of compounded GLP-1 medications — the stock is at $31.66, down 51% from its $65.30 52-week high. A final exclusion could be a negative headline for HIMS but a tailwind for NVO and LLY. The narrative is asymmetric for both directions depending on the outcome and timing.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| HIMS | Hims & Hers — telehealth, compounded GLP-1s | Revenue exposure if compounding banned; stock already impaired |
| NVO | Novo Nordisk — Wegovy/Ozempic | Compounding exclusion = demand redirected to branded |
| LLY | Eli Lilly — Mounjaro/Zepbound | Same demand redirection dynamic |

**What would prove this wrong:** FDA grants a transition period longer than expected. Legal challenge from compounding industry delays enforcement. FDA revises position based on comments (unlikely given the strong stance).

**If this plays out:** HIMS loses a revenue stream (estimated 15-25% of revenue tied to compounded GLP-1s). NVO and LLY see incremental US demand. Compounding pharmacies forced to pivot or shut down GLP-1 lines.

**Key signals to watch:**
- FDA docket FDA-2026-N-XXXX for final Federal Register notice
- Any statements from outsourcing facility associations
- HIMS quarterly earnings for GLP-1 revenue disclosure
- Lawsuits filed by compounding industry

**Sources:**
- [FDA Press Release — Proposed Exclusion](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-proposes-exclude-semaglutide-tirzepatide-and-liraglutide-503b-bulks-list) — April 30, 2026 proposal
- [Federal Register — 503B Bulks List Notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/01/2026-08552/list-of-bulk-drug-substances-for-which-there-is-a-clinical-need-under-section-503b-of-the-federal) — Comment period closed June 30
- [Lachman Consultants Analysis](https://www.lachmanconsultants.com/2026/05/preliminary-decision-to-exclude-certain-glp-1-drugs-from-the-503b-bulks-list/) — FDA standard: clinical need test

---

## 4. DEA Telemedicine Prescribing — Permanent Rule Still Pending

**Event Type:** P2 — Regulatory extension
**Future Catalyst Date:** December 31, 2026 (current extension expires); permanent rule expected before or at expiration
**Time Remaining:** ~5 months

**What happened:** DEA and HHS extended COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances (Schedule II-V) through December 31, 2026 — the fourth temporary extension. The permanent rulemaking process is underway but no proposed rule has been published. The extension allows telehealth prescribing without prior in-person evaluation. DEA has indicated it is "developing permanent regulations" but timeline is unclear.

**Why it matters:** Telehealth platforms (HIMS, Teladoc, etc.) rely on these flexibilities for prescribing controlled substances — particularly ADHD medications, testosterone, and weight management drugs. A permanent rule could either (a) codify flexibilities (bullish for telehealth) or (b) restrict them to specific clinical contexts (bearish). The longer DEA goes without a permanent rule, the more the market assumes extension is the default. This is a P2 because the timeline is wide and the direction is genuinely uncertain. Worth monitoring for a Federal Register proposed rule.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| HIMS | Hims & Hers — telehealth prescribing | Revenue tied to controlled substance prescribing (ADHD, TRT) |
| TDOC | Teladoc — telehealth | Controlled substance prescribing exposure |

**What would prove this wrong:** DEA publishes a proposed permanent rule that broadly preserves current flexibilities (would be a non-event). Congress acts to codify telehealth flexibilities permanently (would remove DEA from the equation).

**If this plays out:** Restrictive permanent rule → telehealth platforms lose prescribing capability for controlled substances → significant revenue impact. Permissive permanent rule → structural tailwind confirmed for telehealth.

**Key signals to watch:**
- Federal Register notices from DEA (search: "telemedicine controlled substances permanent rule")
- DEA/SAMHSA joint statements
- Congressional telehealth bills (legislative alternative)
- HIMS/TDOC lobbying activity disclosures

**Sources:**
- [Federal Register — Fourth Extension](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/12/31/2025-24123/fourth-temporary-extension-of-covid-19-telemedicine-flexibilities-for-prescription-of-controlled) — Extension through Dec 31, 2026
- [DEA Official Statement](https://www.dea.gov/es/node/234606) — Confirmation of extension and permanent rulemaking underway
- [HHS Press Release](https://www.hhs.gov/press-room/dea-telemedicine-extension-2026.html) — Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2026 window

---

## 5. PCAC Meeting — Peptide Compounding (GHK-Cu, Dihexa, Melanotan II)

**Event Type:** P2 — Advisory committee
**Future Catalyst Date:** Before end of February 2027 (FDA stated timeline)
**Time Remaining:** ~6 months

**What happened:** FDA announced it will host a Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) meeting before the end of February 2027 to evaluate five bulk drug substances for the 503A bulks list: Cathelicidin (LL-37), GHK-Cu, Dihexa acetate, Melanotan II, and PEG-MGF. These are popular peptides in the anti-aging, wellness, and grey-market research chemical communities. A Federal Register notice with the specific date and docket is forthcoming.

**Why it matters:** The peptide compounding market is a quietly booming grey economy — med spas, wellness clinics, and telehealth platforms sell compounded peptides (especially GHK-Cu for skin/hair, and various nootropic peptides) to consumers seeking longevity benefits. If PCAC recommends adding these to the 503A bulks list, it legitimizes compounding and is a tailwind. If they're denied (which is the FDA's historical pattern for substances without robust safety data), it disrupts the supply chain for wellness companies. The time horizon is longer (6 months) but this is a structural catalyst for the wellness/longevity compounding ecosystem.

**Direct-impact tickers:** No clean pure-play public tickers — peptide compounding is mostly private (revive, Mochi, etc.). Indirect exposure through HIMS (wellness/telehealth) and compounding pharmacy stocks. Monitoring only.

**What would prove this wrong:** Meeting delayed beyond Q1 2027. FDA removes substances from consideration before the meeting.

**If this plays out:** Denial → peptide supply disruption for med spas / wellness companies. Approval → legitimizes and expands the compounded peptide market.

**Key signals to watch:**
- Federal Register notice with specific PCAC meeting date
- PCAC docket materials (published 2 business days before meeting)
- Public comment submissions (quality and volume)

**Sources:**
- [FDA PCAC Page](https://www.fda.gov/advisory-committees/pharmacy-compounding-advisory-committee/meeting-pharmacy-compounding-advisory-committee) — Meeting before Feb 2027; substances listed

---

_Scan complete. No high-conviction Congressional hearings or novel PDUFA dates flagged this run that meet the asymmetry + narrative-sweet-spot criteria._
